guarantees.claim: u_state_regs (aes_cipher_ctrl_cs) is updated from aes_cipher_ctrl_ns on every clock edge where aes_cipher_ctrl_e is high, and resets to CIPHER_CTRL_IDLE.
rnd_ctr_o is continuously assigned to equal rnd_ctr_q.
The generate block gen_cyc_ctr exists only when elaboration-time parameter SecSBoxImpl equals SBoxImplDom.

assumptions.claim: aes_cipher_ctrl_ns must be a legal one-hot (sparse) encoding for the FSM state vector at all times.
assumptions.cond: when aes_cipher_ctrl_e is high and state update occurs
assumptions.risk: If violated, the FSM may enter an invalid state, causing unpredictable control behavior or violating security properties (no local detection of invalid state).

uncertain_points.claim: The logic inside generate block gen_cyc_ctr (likely a cycle counter) is not included in this chunk. Its effect on rnd_ctr_q and other control signals (e.g., round counting or handshake) cannot be verified without the rest of the block.
uncertain_points.risk: Missing or misbehaving cycle counter could lead to incorrect round termination or data leakage/overwrite.

uncertain_points.claim: The macro PRIM_FLOP_SPARSE_FSM may include an illegal-state checker, but without its full definition it is unknown whether an invalid next-state value (aes_cipher_ctrl_ns) causes a detectable fault (e.g., assertion or alert) or leads to silent corruption of the FSM state.
uncertain_points.cond: when aes_cipher_ctrl_ns is an illegal one-hot value
uncertain_points.risk: If no check exists, a glitch or logic bug could permanently corrupt the control state without detection, potentially enabling unauthorized operations or leaking secret material.
